He sold his remaining stake when L'Oreal acquired the business in 2006.

long_biography.plain_text:
British entrepreneur Ian McGlinn developed a profitable series of six yachts for resale, using common engineering and layouts to shorten delivery times. After completing the first project, he and his advisers calculated whether a second could earn a return. Its commercial promise persuaded him to continue the programme.

His approach combined firm negotiation with an insistence on quality. He would not accept inferior work simply to increase the margin: every project had to meet standards he could live with if it failed to sell. That discipline made his own expectations part of the test for what he offered buyers.
